correctness.rationale: For each prescribed set of r singleton labels there are exactly B_(n-r) remaining partitions; this determines all mixed falling-factorial moments of disjoint windows. Bell's saddle-point formula DLMF 26.7.7 implies B_(n-r)/(B_n a_n^r)->1 for fixed r, a_n=B_(n-1)/B_n and n*a_n->infinity. Thus bounded disjoint left and right windows have independent Poisson limits and the endpoint gaps joint independent Exp(1) limits. The expected-gap statement is not deduced from weak convergence: fourth factorial moments of the singleton count yield an O(lambda^-2) small-count tail; conditioned uniform singleton positions imply exact E[gap]=(n+1)E[1/(S+1)]-1, hence mean-gap scaling. Dobinski gives strict Bell log-convexity and finite positive covariance. All quantifiers, empty-singleton convention, local topology and limits are specified. The standalone enumerator successfully ran 1,106 exact tests, which support bounded cases only; the infinite statements are proved analytically.

originality.rationale: The closest relevant full texts distinguish finite extreme-label identities (Sun and Wu 2010) and component-size-count Poisson approximations (Arratia and Tavare 1994). Neither inspected text asserts independent Poisson processes of rescaled singleton LABEL locations at the two endpoints together with the exact mean-gap asymptotic. Sun–Wu specifically request asymptotics for extreme singleton labels. Classical Bell asymptotics and singleton-marking identities are prior tools, not claimed new. A sufficiently general unlocated historical exchangeable-point-process result might imply this theorem; therefore priority remains conditional, and absence in searches is not treated as uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: A spatial local-Poisson limit might be implicit in earlier random set-partition point-process literature or a broad exchangeable-subset theorem not identified by the searches.

value.rationale: Extreme singleton label locations are a natural parameter-free set-partition statistic explicitly studied in Sun–Wu 2010, whose Remark 3.11 asks for asymptotic mean locations. The theorem gives the first-order n/W(n) gap scale, the stronger joint independent Poisson boundary process, and a contrast with strict finite-n positive dependence. This supplies a structural answer across all fixed boundary windows rather than a routine numeric table or arbitrary sliced invariant. It does not claim a rate or a general theorem for every exchangeable sparse subset.
